title: Job Application and CV / طلب الشغل و السيرة الذاتية
bridge: فالاسبانيول normally we say 'I am 25 years old' or 'I graduated in Tourism', but in English the structure changes: we use the verb 'to have' and specific prepositions like 'in' or 'from'. Also pay attention to the use of 'experience' (not 'experiences' in general contexts) and the placement of the adjective before the noun, which in English is mandatory. Avoid translating 'me dedico a' literally as 'I dedicate myself to', since it sounds too formal; in English we use 'I work as' or 'I am responsible for'.
rule: To talk about your work experience in English at B1 level: 1) Use the simple present to describe your current job: 'I work as a...' (I work as...), 'I am responsible for...' (I am responsible for...). 2) For past experience, use 'used to' or the simple past: 'I used to work at...' / 'I worked at...'. 3) The verb 'have' is used to express age and possession of skills: 'I have five years of experience' (I have five years of experience). 4) Adjectives go before the noun: 'I have strong communication skills' (not 'skills strong'). 5) Use 'in' for sectors ('experience in hospitality'), 'at' for companies ('at a hotel'), and 'as' for positions ('as a manager'). 6) In the CV, bullet points are used with verbs in the past or present, not full sentences.

title: Discussing current events / نتحادثو على الأخبار و الأحداث الجارية
bridge: فـي الإسبانـيول، كتير بغينا نستخدم الزمن الحاضر البسيط أو الماضي البسيط علشان نحكيو الأخبار، و عبارات زاي 'según' أو 'dicen que'. فـالإنجليزي، العادة باش نخدمو الزمن الحاضر التام (present perfect) علشان الأخبار الجديدة (مثال: 'has happened')، و الماضي البسيط علشان التفاصيل المحددة. بالإضافة، الزمن المستمر (present continuous) كتير مستعمل فـالإنجليزي علشان_actions اللي فـالتطور (مثال: 'is happening'). خطأ شائع هو الترجمة الحرفية لـ'está pasando' بـ'is happening'، بينما فـالإنجليزي، كنخدمو الزمن الحاضر البسيط علشان الحقائق العامة.
rule: علشان تحكي الأخبار فـالإنجليزي فـمستوى B1: 1. خدم الزمن الحاضر التام (have/has + past participle) علشان تخبر خبر جديد من غير وقت محدد: 'Scientists have discovered a new planet.' 2. خدم الماضي البسيط علشان التفاصيل مع وقت محدد: 'They announced the result yesterday.' 3. خدم الزمن الحاضر المستمر علشان الأفعال اللي فـالتطور دلوقتي: 'The government is debating the new law.' 4. علشان تعبر عن رأيك، خدم عبارات زاي 'I think', 'In my opinion', 'I believe' متبوعة بجملة. 5. مصطلحات مهمة: 'headline', 'article', 'report', 'according to', 'latest', 'issue'.

title: Cultural Differences and Misunderstandings / الفروق الثقافية وسوء الفهم
bridge: فـي الإسـبـانـيـة، نـعـبّـر عـن الإزعـاج أو الـدهـشـة بـشـكـل أكـثـر مـبـاشـرة، فـي حـيـن أنـه فـي الإـنـجـلـيـزيـة نـلـجـأ إلـى لـغـة غـيـر مـبـاشـرة و مـؤدّبـة أكـثـر، مـثـل 'I think...' أو 'Maybe...'. كـمـا أنـه فـي الإـنـجـلـيـزيـة نـحـلّ سـوء الفهـم عـادة بـواسـطـة أسـئـلـة تـأكـيـد ('Do you mean...?')، فـي حـيـن أنـه فـي الإسـبـانـيـة نـفـتـرض أو نـقـاطـع. لـتـفـادي الـنـزاعـات، مـن الـمـهـم تـعـلـم طـلـب التوضـيـحـات بـجـمـل مـثـل 'What do you mean?' بـدلاً مـن افـتـراض أنـك فـهـمـت. هـذا يـنـطـبـق كـذلـك عـلـى اسـتـعـمـال الـزمـن، فـفـي الإـنـجـلـيـزيـة نـسـتـعـمـل الـمـاضـي الـبـسـيـط لـلأفـعـال الـمـنـتـهـاة، فـي حـيـن أنـه فـي الإسـبـانـيـة نـسـتـعـمـل فـي الـبـعـض الـمـاضـي الـمـركـب لـلأحـداث الـقـريـبـة.
rule: عـلـى مـسـتـوى B1، لـلـتـحـدّث عـن الفـروق الـثـقـافـيـة وسـوء الفهـم بـالإنـجـلـيـزيـة، مـن الـمـهـم إجـادة: 1) الأسـئـلـة غـيـر الـمـبـاشـرة: 'Could you explain that?' بـدلاً مـن 'Explain that'. 2) تـعـبـيـر الـرأي بـشـكـل مـلـيـن: 'I think', 'I feel', 'I guess' لـتـفـادي الـصـراحـة الـمـفـرطـة. 3) أسـئـلـة التـأكـيـد: 'Do you mean...?', 'Are you saying...?' لـتـأكـيـد مـا قـالـه الـشـخـص. 4) اسـتـعـمـال الـمـاضـي الـبـسـيـط لـلأفـعـال الـمـنـتـهـاة: 'I misunderstood' (مـثـل 'I have misunderstood' إذا لـم يـكـن لـلـحـالـي صـلـة بـالـمـضـي). تـجـنـب الـتـرجـمـة الـحـرفـيـة لـ'تـمـتـع بـالـحـق' (to be right، لـيـس 'to have reason') و لـ'يـحـتـاج' (to need، لـيـس 'to make lack').

title: Discussing Environmental Topics / Hablando sobre temas medioambientales
bridge: F spanjoli, bghit n3ibdu l7al li kayn f lwa9t dyalo, 3ndna nkhdmu b hada l7al lmob9at l3adya ('contaminamos') aw lmob9at lmstmirra ('estamos contaminando') bla far9. F l3nglizi, had ltimayuz kayn 3la dima: lmob9at l3adya ('we pollute') kay3ibdu 3la 3ada bhal ma kayn f l7al li kayn 3la dima, while lmob9at lmstmirra ('we are polluting') kay3ibdu 3la l7al li kayn kayt3ml f had lwa9t. 3ndema, f l3nglizi, bghit n7ddu 3la l7al li kayn f lmustaqbal lmukhtat (bhal 'We are going to reduce waste'), kaykhdmu b 'be going to' aw lmob9at lmstmirra, while f spanjoli 3adtnan nkhdmu b lmustaqbal l3adya ('reduciremos'). 9ddem 3la 9iyadtk b 'should' bhal ma kayn f spanjoli 3adtnan nkhdmu b 'deberíamos'.
rule: Bhal ma kayn f spanjoli, bghit n7ddu 3la l7al li kayn f lmob9at l3adya (3ada: 'The planet is warming' – 3ndema kaykhdmu b lmob9at lmstmirra 3la 7ssab ma kayn 7al; bhal ma kayn f l7al: 'Climate change affects everyone'), 2) lmob9at lmstmirra (7al li kayn kayt3ml: 'Forests are disappearing'), 3) 'be going to' + fi3l (mukhtat lmustaqbal: 'We are going to install solar panels'), w 4) 'should' + fi3l (twsiyat: 'You should recycle more'). 3ndema kayn f l3nglizi, lmob9at l3adya kayt3ml b '-s' f l3adad lwa7d (he/she/it). Bhal ma kayn f 'there is/are' (kayna), 3ndema 'there is' bhal ma kayn 7al, 'there are' bhal ma kayn jma3. 3ndema kaykhdmu b l9awtib bhal 'because', 'so', 'therefore' bhal ma kayn f l7al. Ma tensa3x 3la 7al li l9adad kayn qbl l7arf f l3nglizi ('renewable energy', ma kayn 'energy renewable').

concept_examples.text: We are reducing our carbon footprint by using public transport.
concept_examples.translation: Kan3ddu 7assabtnna f lkharj l3adwi b nkhdmu b lmowasel l3amma.
concept_examples.phonetic: /wiː ɑːr rɪˈdjuːsɪŋ ˈaʊər ˈkɑːrbən ˈfʊtprɪnt baɪ ˈjuːzɪŋ ˈpʌblɪk ˈtrænspɔːrt/

concept_examples.text: Climate change affects everyone, but we can still make a difference.
concept_examples.translation: Tghyyr l7al lklimayti kay3tbr 3la l7ad, walakin 3ndna 3nd lmumkin n7dddu f lfarq.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ˈklaɪmət tʃeɪndʒ əˈfɛkts ˈɛvriwʌn, bʌt wiː kæn stɪl meɪk ə ˈdɪfərəns/

concept_examples.text: If we don't act now, the planet will suffer serious consequences.
concept_examples.translation: Lma kan3mlu 7al lwa9t hada, lkura ykhdm 3la 3aqibat khatira.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɪf wiː doʊnt ækt naʊ, ðə ˈplænɪt wɪl ˈsʌfər ˈsɪriəs ˈkɒnsɪkwənsɪz/

concept_examples.text: You should replace plastic bags with reusable ones.

concept_examples.phonetic: /juː ʃʊd rɪˈpleɪs ˈplæstɪk bæɡz wɪð riːˈjuːzəbəl wʌnz/

common_error.wrong: We are recycle the plastic bottles in our house.
common_error.correct: We recycle the plastic bottles in our house.
common_error.correct_alt: We are recycling the plastic bottles in our house.
common_error.explanation: Lkhata' kayn 3la 7asas lkhtalat bin lmob9at l3adya w lmob9at lmstmirra. F spanjoli, 'reciclamos' kaykhdmu bhal ma kayn 3ada aw 7al li kayn kayt3ml f lwa9t hada. F l3nglizi, lma yakun 3ada aw rutina, kaykhdmu b lmob9at l3adya ('recycle'); lma yakun 7al li kayn kayt3ml f lwa9t hada, kaykhdmu b lmob9at lmstmirra ('are recycling'). Ma kayn 3ndha 'are recycle' – lfi3l l3asli ykhdm b '-ing' f lmob9at lmstmirra.

examples.original: Air pollution is a serious problem in many cities.
examples.phonetic: /ɛər pəˈluːʃən ɪz ə ˈsɪriəs ˈprɒbləm ɪn ˈmɛni ˈsɪtiz/

examples.original: The oceans are getting warmer because of climate change.
examples.phonetic: /ðə ˈoʊʃənz ɑːr ˈɡɛtɪŋ ˈwɔːrmər bɪˈkɒz əv ˈklaɪmət tʃeɪndʒ/
examples.note: Khdm b lmob9at lmstmirra 'are getting' bhal ma kayn 7al li kayn kayt3ml.

examples.original: There is too much plastic waste in the environment.

examples.translation: Kayna 7ta 7ta mn lmukhalat lplastik f lbi'ah.
examples.note: Khdm b 'there is' m3a l7al li ma kayn 3adad bhal 'waste'. Ma tqwl 'there are waste'.

examples.original: Deforestation destroys the habitat of many animals.

examples.translation: Lghrs lhajar ykhdm 3la lmakan li kayn fih 7ta mn l7ayawan.
examples.note: Lmob9at l3adya bhal ma kayn 7al 3adya. 3ndema l'-s' f l3adad lwa7d: 'destroys'.

examples.original: We are planting more trees in our neighborhood.
examples.phonetic: /wiː ɑːr ˈplæntɪŋ mɔːr triːz ɪn ˈaʊər ˈneɪbərhʊd/
examples.note: Lmob9at lmstmirra bhal ma kayn 7al li kayn kayt3ml. 'Plant' kayt3ddl 3la 'planting'.

examples.original: Our school is going to start a recycling program.
examples.phonetic: /ˈaʊər skuːl ɪz ˈɡoʊɪŋ tə stɑːrt ə riːˈsaɪklɪŋ ˈproʊɡræm/
examples.note: Khdm b 'be going to' bhal ma kayn mukhtat lmustaqbal. 3ndema 'is going to' f l7adit l3adya.

examples.original: We should use less electricity to save energy.
examples.phonetic: /wiː ʃʊd juːz lɛs ɪlɛkˈtrɪsɪti tə seɪv ˈɛnərdʒi/
examples.translation: Ylzim 3lik nkhdmu b lkharj lkalil bhal ma kayn nkhddu 3la l7arara.
examples.note: 'Should' m3a lfi3l m3a 'to'. 'Less' bhal ma kayn 3adad; 'fewer' bhal ma kayn jma3.

examples.original: If everyone recycles, we will reduce pollution.
examples.phonetic: /ɪf ˈɛvriwʌn riːˈsaɪkəlz, wiː wɪl rɪˈdjuːs pəˈluːʃən/

examples.note: Lshartiya l1: 'if' + lmob9at l3adya, 'will' + fi3l. 'Everyone' kayn 7al.

examples.original: I think that electric cars are a good investment for the future.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ θɪŋk ðæt ɪˈlɛktrɪk kɑːrz ɑːr ə ɡʊd ɪnˈvɛstmənt fɔːr ðə ˈfjuːtʃər/
examples.translation: Kan3taqid 3la 7ssab li l7ayarat lkahrba kayn 3adad mzyan lmustaqbal.
examples.note: Khdm b 'I think that' bhal ma kayn rayn. 3ndema ba3d 'think', l9awtib 'that' ma kayn 3adad.

examples.original: In my opinion, recycling should be mandatory in every city.
examples.phonetic: /ɪn maɪ əˈpɪnjən, riːˈsaɪklɪŋ ʃʊd biː ˈmændətəri ɪn ˈɛvri ˈsɪti/

examples.original: The government should invest more in renewable energy sources.

title: Talking About Technology and Social Media /Talking About Technology and Social Media
bridge: F l-inglizi, bghit nkhdm b l-ḥāl l-mabsūṭ l-ʿādī l-bnāy l-ʿādāt u b l-ʿamaliyāt l-qāyima (mṯl: 'hādā l-waqt bghit nṣūf l-mākīn'), mā-ʿāndhūmš l-farq bn l-ḥāl l-mabsūṭ u l-ḥāl l-mustamirr b l-inglizi. Kīfā, mṯl mā-nṭqū l-ḥāla l-ʿilmiyya l-tiknūlūjiyya, l-ḥad l-mutakallimīn b l-lugha l-espanyūliyya yʿāwdo ynaqlū bn l-qāyidāt mṯl 'ḥta l-nqīṭ' u 'ḥta nṣūf l-ṣūra', mā-ʿāndhūmš f l-inglizi 'I have to click' u 'I like the photo' bla l-ḍamīr 'me'. Khāṣṣk tnṣar f l-ʿabārāt l-murakkaba (mṯl: 'log in', 'sign up') lli mā-ʿāndhūmš tlaqqāb d-dīrāz mṯl l-espanyūl, u bghīt tṭarjamū b fʿal wāḥd.
rule: L-ḥta nṭqū l-ḥāla l-ʿilmiyya l-tiknūlūjiyya u l-shabakat l-ijtimāʿiyya b l-inglizi b-mustawā B1, khāṣṣk tḥdd: 1) l-ḥāl l-mabsūṭ l-ʿādī l-bnāy l-ʿādāt u l-ḥāla (I check my phone every morning). 2) l-ḥāl l-mustamirr l-bnāy l-ʿamaliyāt l-qāyima (I am scrolling through Instagram right now). 3) l-ʿafʿāl l-mudāfʿa l-bnāy l-taswīyāt u l-qudra: can, should, must (You should update your password). 4) l-ʿabārāt l-murakkaba l-shāʿa: log in, log out, sign up, turn on, turn off, set up. 5) l-taʿbīrāt mʿ l-'like' u 'share' (I like the post, She shared the video). Khāṣṣk tʿlām l-ḥta mā-ʿāndhūmš l-ʿarf l-qasamī bn 'social media' (I spend time on social media, mā-ʿāndhūmš 'in the social media'). Khāṣṣṣk l-ḥta nʿbbr ʿn l-milkīyya mʿ l-ʿalāqāt nḥt l-'have' (I have a new phone) u mā-ʿāndhūmš 'tengo' b l-maʿnā d-'there is'.

L-ḥta tjtjnb hād l-khaṭa, khāṣṣk tʿlām l-ḥta 'agree' mā-ʿāndhūmš 'be' qddām. Khāṣṣṣk kīfā nqūl 'I am agree', l-ṣaḥīḥ hwa 'I agree'. title: Talking about Education and Studying Abroad / التربية ودراسة بالخارج
bridge: فِي الإِنجليزي، نِتْكَلَّم عَن المُسْتَقْبَل بْالحاضِر أو بْالمُسْتَقْبَل البسيط ("I am studying", "I will study"), لكن فِيهِمْ كَيْفَ يِسْتَخْدِمُوا الحاضِر المُسْتَمِرّ ("I am studying") لْمَعْنى مُسْتَقْبَل عِنْدَما يَكُون فِيهِ خُطَّة مُحَدَّدَة. كَمَا فِيهِمْ كَيْفَ يِقُولُوا "I am 20 years old" مَعْنى "عندي 20 عام"، مَعْنى "I have 20 years" مَشْ مِعْقُول. عِنْدَما نِتْكَلَّم عَن الدِّرَاسَة، نِلاَحِظ أنَّ أَسْمَاء المَوَادّ وْحُقُول الدِّرَاسَة مَايْجِيشْ فِيهِمْ "ال" ("I study mathematics")، عَكْس الإِسباني ("Estudio las matemáticas"). خُذْ هَادِ الفَرْق فِيهِمْ حَتَّى تِتْكَلَّم بِطَبْعِيَّة أَكْثَر.
rule: عَشان تِتْكَلَّم عَن الدِّرَاسَة وْدراسة بالخارج فِالإِنجليزي بمُسْتَوَى B1، خُذْ هَادِ القَوَاعِد: 1. الحاضِر البسيط لْحَقَائِق وْعَادَات ("I study every day"). 2. الحاضِر المُسْتَمِرّ لْأَفْعَال جَارِيَة ("I am studying for my exam") وْخُطَط مُسْتَقْبَلِيَّة مُحَدَّدَة ("I am going to England next month"). 3. "Going to" لْنيَّات ("I'm going to apply for a scholarship"). 4. "Will" لْقَرَارَات العَفْوِيَّة أو التَّنَبُّؤَات ("I think it will be a great experience"). 5. الأَفْعَال المِثَالِيَّة مِثْل "can", "must", "should" لْمَهَارَات وْالواجِبَات وْالنَّصَائِح ("You should apply early"). 6. حُرُوف الجَرّ: "study at a university", "apply for a course", "major in" (تخصص فِيهِ)، "take an exam". 7. أَسْمَاء المَوَادّ مَعْندِيشْ "ال" ("I like history"). 8. خُذْ "abroad" (بالخارج) مَعْندِيشْ حَرْف جَرّ، لكن "to study abroad" أو "study abroad" كْفِعْل أو اسْم.

title: Talking about Past Trips and Travel Experiences / Hablando de viajes y experiencias pasadas
bridge: F spanol, bgha ntkalmu 3la tjawrat li msa mn 9bal, kanst3mlu hada dyal lmadi 3la l7al, lmadi lm3raf 3la 'ana 7ayt safart' dyal lmadi lm3raf 3la 'safart' kaykon bghit mn lsiyaq lwa9ti. F nnglizi, had lfar9 bgha ykoun bhal bzaf mn l7al mn 9bal, lmadi lm3raf (have + past participle) kaykun 3la tjawrat bla wa9t m3ayyan, 9ad lmadi lm3raf (past simple) kaykun 3la 3malat fi wa9t m3ayyan fi lmadi. 3a9ba 9adim kaykon kay7el 3la lmadi lm3raf mn 9bal lmadi lm3raf 3ndma kantaslu 3la 'wsh 7ayt 7ayt...?', 3la 7sab an spanol kaykun 'has estado' mn 9bal, mn 9ad lmadi kaykun 3ndma kantaslu 'have you ever been'. 3ndma lmadi lm3raf kaykun 'go/went/gone' dyal 'see/saw/seen' kaykun 3ndhom mn lm3raf, ltalaba nnglizi kaykun 3ndhom lm3raf mn l7al 3ndma kaykon 3ndhom lm3raf mn l7al 'been' dyal 'gone': 'have been' kay3ni 'dayer 3la lmr w rja3', 9ad 'have gone' kay3ni 'kaykun hna l7al dayer'.
rule: Bgha ntkalmu 3la tjawrat safar f nnglizi f darja B1, 3ndk 2 lwa9t rysisn: lmadi lm3raf (have/has + past participle) dyal lmadi lm3raf (past simple). 3st3ml lmadi lm3raf 3la: 1) tjawrat 3omriya bla wa9t m3ayyan (I have visited Paris), 2) m3a adverbs 3la 'ever', 'never', 'already', 'yet' (Have you ever been to Japan?), 3) 3malat li badat fi lmadi w 3awdha tstamr (I have lived here for three years). 3st3ml lmadi lm3raf 3la: 1) 3malat li tamamt fi wa9t m3ayyan fi lmadi (I visited Paris last summer), 2) m3a expressions dyal wa9t 3la 'yesterday', 'in 2019', 'last week', 'when I was a child'. Lmadi lm3raf shwiya li kaykon 3la tjawrat: go-went-gone, see-saw-seen, eat-ate-eaten, take-took-taken, fly-flew-flown, ride-rode-ridden, drive-drove-driven, stay-stayed-stayed (regular). Lbnya lm3raf f lmadi lm3raf: Have/Has + subject + past participle? (Have you ever flown first class?). Ljawab lm3raf: Yes, I have / No, I haven't. F lmadi lm3raf: Did + subject + base verb? (Did you go to the beach?). Ljawab lm3raf: Yes, I did / No, I didn't. M3a 'ever' dyal 'never' kaykun lmadi lm3raf, msh lmadi lm3raf: 'I have never been to Mexico' (mash 'I never went to Mexico' 3ndma kaykun tjawra 3omriya). Ma t9dsh 'since' m3a n9ta 3la lwa9t li msa (I have visited Spain since 2018 - msh 7al 9ad lwa9t m3ayyan), 3st3ml 'since' m3a lbdya dyal 3malat mstamra (I have been in Spain since 2018). 3ndk an ladjectives dyal rai (amazing, terrible, wonderful, boring) kaykun 3st3ml m3a 'was/were' f lmadi lm3raf 3la t9sir lm3rifa.

title: Talking about habits and routines / التحدث عن العادات والروتينات
bridge: فـي الإنگليزي normally we use simple present to talk about habits like in English, but there are important differences: in English, simple present needs 'do/does' as auxiliary for negation and questions, while in Spanish we use 'no' or inversion without auxiliary. Also, frequency adverbs (always, usually, etc.) come before the main verb, but after the verb 'to be', which doesn’t happen in Spanish. Watch out for the 's' in third person (he/she/it), which is easy to forget for Spanish speakers.
rule: To talk about habits and routines in English, use present simple. For third person singular (he, she, it), add -s or -es to the verb (e.g., 'works', 'goes'). For negation, use 'do not' (don't) or 'does not' (doesn't) + base verb. For questions, use 'do' or 'does' at the beginning, followed by subject and base verb. Frequency adverbs (always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely, never) are placed: (1) before main verb (I always drink coffee), (2) after 'to be' (He is always late), and (3) between auxiliary and verb in questions/negations (Do you often exercise?). Exceptions: with 'have' as main verb, use 'have/has' (I have breakfast at 8). With 'go' and 'do', third person changes to 'goes' and 'does'. For actions in progress now, don’t use present simple; use present continuous.

title: Making Plans and Invitations / 3adad lkhawater w d3wa
bridge: F l-nglizy, 3ashan n3addu lkhawater w d3wa, 3ndna bnyat 3la shkl 'would you like to...?' aw 'how about...?', lli ma 3ndhomsh m3akel m3aya f l-3rbiyya. 3ndna 7ta af3al m3 l-3barat 3la shkl 'hang out' lli kaykunu shya bzaf f n-nqashat l-3adiya. 3ayni 3la shi haja: l-nglizy kayst3mlu l-m3ad 7al l-mustaqbal b l-3amal l-mustqbl (I'm meeting) 3la 7sab l-3rbiyya kayst3mlu 7ta l-m3ad l-basit (Quedo).
rule: 3ashan n3addu l-d3wa, 3ndna: 'Would you like to + fi3l?' (m3akel) aw 'Do you want to + fi3l?' (3adi). 3ashan nqaddmu tawsiya: 'How about + l-masdar?' aw 'What about + l-masdar?'. 3ashan nqblu: 'Sure', 'Sounds good', 'I'd love to'. 3ashan nqllu: 'I'm afraid I can't', 'Sorry, I have other plans'. 3ashan l-mustaqbal, 3ndna l-m3ad l-mustqbl (I'm meeting my friends tomorrow) aw 'going to' (I'm going to visit my sister). L-fi3l 'hang out' 3ni y3ni nqdiw wa7t m3 l-7wayej b r-ra7a. 3ayni 3la shi haja: ma n3adduhsh m3aya b l-3amal '¿Quedamos?' 3la shkl 'Are we staying?', l-7aqiqiya hiya 'Shall we meet?' aw 'Let's meet up'.

concept_examples.translation: Bghiti nmshiw l-sinima l-llila hada?
concept_examples.phonetic: /wʊd juː laɪk tə ɡoʊ tə ðə ˈmuːviz təˈnaɪt/

concept_examples.text: How about hanging out at the park on Saturday?
concept_examples.translation: Shnu 3la l-hsab nqdiw l-3amara f l-had l-3ashiya?
concept_examples.phonetic: /haʊ əˈbaʊt ˈhæŋɪŋ aʊt æt ðə pɑːrk ɒn ˈsætərdeɪ/

concept_examples.text: Sure, sounds great!
concept_examples.translation: 3afak, 3jaba hdak l-7al!
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʃʊr saʊndz ɡreɪt/

concept_examples.text: I'm afraid I can't make it; I have other plans.
concept_examples.translation: Khafi 3liya ma nqdirsh, 3ndi 7wayej 3khrin.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪm əˈfreɪd aɪ kænt meɪk ɪt aɪ hæv ˈʌðər plænz/

common_error.explanation: L-khta2 kaykunu mn t3adud l-3rabiyya '¿Quedamos?' 3la shkl 'Are we staying?', 3la 7sab 'staying' 3ni 'l-3aqa' aw 'l-ttawul'. examples.original: Do you want to grab a coffee sometime?

examples.original: What about watching a series tonight?

examples.note: 'What about' + l-masdar hiya shya m3ada l-twasiyya.

examples.original: How about going to the beach this weekend?
examples.phonetic: /haʊ əˈbaʊt ˈɡoʊɪŋ tə ðə biːtʃ ðɪs ˌwiːkˈend/
examples.translation: Shnu 3la l-hsab nmshiw l-sh8al had l-3am?
examples.note: 'How about' y 'what about' son intercambiables en sugerencias.

examples.original: We could hang out after the meeting.
examples.phonetic: /wiː kʊd hæŋ aʊt ˈæftər ðə ˈmiːtɪŋ/
examples.note: 'Could' 3ni y3ni l-imkan w kayl9a l-twasiyya.

examples.original: I'd love to, but I'm busy on Sunday.

examples.note: 'I'd love to' 3ni y3ni l-7ub l-masdar, 3la 7sab 'but' l-tqyid.

examples.original: That sounds fun! Let's do it.
examples.phonetic: /ðæt saʊndz fʌn lɛts duː ɪt/
examples.note: 'Let's do it' hiya 7al l-qabul l-mththth.

examples.original: Sorry, I can't. Maybe another time.

examples.note: 'Maybe another time' kayl9a l-rfu3 w ykhli l-bab mftu7.

concept_examples.translation: Sbah lxir, lyoum ġadi nhddu mʕa lmuhimiyya dyal lrecyclage.

concept_examples.text: Firstly, recycling helps reduce waste in our cities.
concept_examples.translation: Bda, lrecyclage kay3awn 3la tnxif dyal lmuxatir f mdinetna.

concept_examples.text: To conclude, we all should recycle more to protect the planet.

examples.original: Good morning, everyone.
examples.phonetic: /ɡʊd ˈmɔːrnɪŋ ˈevriwʌn/
examples.note: Slaam rasmi bhal ma kaykon l7al.

examples.original: I'd like to start by talking about...
examples.phonetic: /aɪd laɪk tə stɑːrt baɪ ˈtɔːkɪŋ əbaʊt/
examples.note: Frase útil para introducir el tema. Se usa 'I'd like' para ser educado y formal.

examples.original: Let me begin with a quick introduction.
examples.phonetic: /let mi bɪˈɡɪn wɪð ə kwɪk ˌɪntrəˈdʌkʃən/
examples.note: Alternativa para abrir. 'Let me' significa 'déjame', es una manera directa pero cortés.

examples.original: Firstly, let's look at the benefits.
examples.phonetic: /ˈfɜːrstli lets lʊk æt ðə ˈbenɪfɪts/
examples.note: 'Firstly' kaybdaw bhal ma kaykon l7al.

examples.original: Secondly, I want to mention some challenges.
examples.phonetic: /ˈsekəndli aɪ wɑːnt tə ˈmenʃən sʌm ˈtʃælɪndʒɪz/
examples.translation: Bzaf, ġadi ndkhl f ba3d l3aqab.
examples.note: 'Secondly' kaybdaw l7al.

examples.original: Another important point is that...
examples.phonetic: /əˈnʌðər ɪmˈpɔːrtənt pɔɪnt ɪz ðæt/
examples.note: Alternativa bhal ma kaykon l7al.

examples.original: However, we must consider the costs.
examples.phonetic: /haʊˈevər wi mʌst kənˈsɪdər ðə kɔːsts/
examples.note: 'However' kaybdaw l7al.

examples.original: In conclusion, I'd like to summarize the main points.
examples.phonetic: /ɪn kənˈkluːʒən aɪd laɪk tə ˈsʌməraɪz ðə meɪn pɔɪnts/
examples.translation: Bhal xatima, ġadi nġawlu l3aks lmuhim.
examples.note: 'In conclusion' rasmi, bzaf mnin kaykon l7al.

examples.original: To wrap up, remember that every small action counts.
examples.phonetic: /tə ræp ʌp rɪˈmembər ðæt ˈevri smɔːl ˈækʃən kaʊnts/
examples.translation: Bhal xatima, dkhlu f balkum bnna kl tasʕir kay3awn.
examples.note: 'To wrap up' kaybdaw l7al.

examples.original: Thank you for your attention.
examples.phonetic: /θæŋk ju fɔːr jʊər əˈtenʃən/
examples.note: Lchukran l7al kaykon l7al.
